channel.title: Fintech Tunisia (EN)
channel.description: Independent, sourced reporting on fintech in Tunisia and across Africa.

item.title: Tunisia Fintech Ecosystem Map: Who's Who in 2026
item.description: From the BCT to Ooredoo's new payment institution, Konnect and the ANAVA fund of funds: a practical map of who does what in Tunisian fintech.

item.title: Tunisia Startup Funding Trends 2024–2026: Boom, Then Freeze
item.description: After $39 million in 2025, Tunisian startups recorded almost no disclosed equity deals in the first half of 2026. Here is what the numbers show.

item.title: Payment Institutions in Tunisia: Licensing and the 2026 Rules
item.description: The Central Bank of Tunisia has replaced its 2018 payment institution rules with a far stricter circular. Here is how the licence works and what changes.

item.title: Mobile Payments in Tunisia: The Wallet Landscape in 2026
item.description: Tunisia's mobile wallets are multiplying, from bank apps and La Poste to fintechs and telecom operators. The usage numbers are rising quickly but remain small next to cards and cash.

item.title: Tunisia's Startup Act Explained: What Fintech Founders Get
item.description: The 2018 Startup Act brings real tax, social-security and foreign-currency benefits. Here is who qualifies, what you get and why the label is not a fintech licence.

item.title: The BCT Regulatory Sandbox: How Tunisia Tests Fintech
item.description: Launched in 2020, the Central Bank of Tunisia's sandbox lets fintechs test products with real users under supervision. Here is what it has done so far, and what it cannot do.

item.title: E-commerce Payments in Tunisia: ClicToPay to Cash on Delivery
item.description: Online payments in Tunisia are growing fast, but most shoppers still pay cash at the door. Here is how merchants can accept payments online and what each option involves.

item.title: AI in Tunisian Banking: Real Uses, Rules and Gaps
item.description: Chatbots, remote identity checks and credit scoring are the first AI uses in Tunisian banks. There is no AI-specific rulebook yet, and that cuts both ways for founders.

item.title: Tunisia's Cash Economy: Record Banknotes, Fading Cheques
item.description: More than TND 30 billion in banknotes and coins now circulate in Tunisia, a record. The cheque reform, informality and low bank account ownership explain why the cashless push is struggling.

item.title: ANAVA Fund of Funds Explained: Tunisia's VC Engine
item.description: Backed by the World Bank, CDC and KfW, the ANAVA fund of funds is behind most seed capital in Tunisia. Here is how it works and who it backs.

item.title: AfCFTA, Digital Trade and Cross-Border Payments in Africa
item.description: Africa adopted a Digital Trade Protocol in 2024 with annexes on payments, data and fintech. It is not yet in force. Here is what it covers and why Tunisia should care.

item.title: Instant Payments in Tunisia: Switching and Interoperability
item.description: Tunisians can send money instantly between some mobile wallets, but bank transfers still clear in batches and there is no national instant payment system. The BCT is studying Brazil's Pix.

item.title: Diaspora Remittances to Tunisia: Volumes, Costs, Digital Channels
item.description: Tunisians abroad sent home TND 8.76 billion through formal channels in 2025, more than tourism brought in. Sending money is getting cheaper online, but cash and informal channels still dominate.

item.title: Expensya's Acquisition by Medius: A Tunisian Exit Story
item.description: Founded in Tunis in 2014, Expensya was acquired by Sweden's Medius in 2023. How the exit happened and what it means for Tunisian founders.

item.title: Flouci: Profile of Tunisia's Mobile Wallet and Banking App
item.description: Founded as Kaoun in 2018, Flouci has become one of Tunisia's best-known fintech apps, combining a wallet, a bank account opened remotely and merchant payments.

item.title: African Fintech Funding 2025–2026: Debt, Megadeals, Fewer Deals
item.description: African tech funding recovered in 2025, but fintech's share is shrinking, debt is rising and deal counts hit new lows in H1 2026. Here is what the numbers say.

item.title: Tunisia Fintech Key Numbers: Accounts, Cards, Mobile, Cash
item.description: Fewer than four in ten adults have an account, mobile payments grew 80% in 2025, and cash keeps rising. The essential, sourced figures on Tunisian fintech.

item.title: Crowdfunding Law in Tunisia: How the CMF Framework Works
item.description: Six years after Law 2020-37, Tunisia's equity crowdfunding rules are complete and the first platform licence has been granted. Here is what founders need to know.

item.title: La Poste Tunisienne's e-Dinar and D17 Explained
item.description: Long before fintech apps, Tunisia's post office offered e-Dinar cards for online payment. Its D17 app now competes with banks and startups in a crowded wallet market.

item.title: Cybersecurity in Tunisia's Financial Sector: The New Rules
item.description: BCT circular 2026-10 and Decree-law 2023-17 make security audits, incident reporting and strong remote identity checks mandatory for Tunisian payment fintechs.

item.title: Financial Inclusion in Tunisia: What the Findex Data Says
item.description: Tunisia's account ownership rate has barely moved since 2017. The latest Findex data shows who is left out, and why cash still dominates.

item.title: How to Raise Funding as a Tunisian Fintech: A 2026 Guide
item.description: From the Startup Act label to Series A, a step-by-step guide to raising money as a Tunisian fintech, with real ticket sizes and pitfalls.

item.title: Konnect Networks: Profile of a Tunisian Payments Startup
item.description: Founded in 2021, Konnect Networks built a payment gateway for Tunisian merchants, raised money from Visa and Attijariwafa Ventures, and now pitches itself as infrastructure for banks, payment institutions and telcos.

item.title: Africa's Fintech Unicorns: Moniepoint, OPay, Wave and More
item.description: Almost every African unicorn is a fintech. Who they are, how reliable their valuations are, and why none of them is Tunisian.

item.title: Tunisia Incubators and Accelerators for Fintech Founders
item.description: From Flat6Labs' seed tickets to bank-run labs and Visa's African fintech accelerator: where Tunisian fintech founders can find support, and how to choose.

item.title: Crypto Regulation in Tunisia: Is Bitcoin Legal in 2026?
item.description: Tunisia has no crypto law, but the foreign exchange code makes holding and trading crypto legally risky. Draft reforms would change that, if adopted.

item.title: Digital Banking in Tunisia: Where Banks Stand in 2026
item.description: Mobile payments grew 80.5% in 2025 and new rules allow remote onboarding, but most Tunisian adults still have no account. A look at banks' digital shift.

item.title: Microfinance in Tunisia: Enda Tamweel, Taysir and the ACM
item.description: More than 800,000 Tunisians borrow from microfinance institutions. A look at the rules, the main lenders, the cost of credit and the new cap on excessive rates.

item.title: InstaDeep and BioNTech: Lessons for Tunisian Tech
item.description: Founded in Tunis with two laptops, InstaDeep was bought by BioNTech for up to £562 million. What the deal teaches Tunisian tech and fintech founders.

item.title: Paymee: Profile of a Tunisian Payment Pioneer Under Pressure
item.description: Paymee helped Tunisian merchants accept card payments online and at delivery. A 2023 anti-money laundering freeze, later linked to a regulatory grey zone, put the company at risk.
